newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DOMESTIC DEBT FALLS TO 2.484 TRLN LEVS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DOMESTIC DEBT FALLS TO 2.484 TRLN LEVS.

text.p: Bulgaria's domestic debt fell by 294 billion levs in March to 2.484 trillion levs mainly because of the lev appreciation, a central bank official said on Wednesday.

"Domestic debt fell due to the lev rise, which diminished the price of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds and deposit guarantee bonds," Nikolina Micheva, head of State Credits department at the central bank told Reuters.

Net sales of government securities in March totalled around 194 billion levs while the lev rise erased some 486 billion levs off the value of dollar-denominated government securities, Finance ministry figures showed.

The lev gained to 1,588.8 per dollar on March 31 from 2,045.5 on February 28 in the central bank daily fixing used in the calculations as the interim cabinet launched urgent stabilisation measures and won funding pledges from international lenders.
The lev traded near 1,500 per dollar on the local interbank market on Wednesday.
Finance ministry's direct loans from the Bulgarian National Bank and the State Savings Bank fell by 270 million levs to 138.515 billion levs in March.

The ministry issued $79.2 million of floater coupon T-bonds last year to guarantee foreign currency deposits of companies and individuals in five local banks against which the central bank has filed insolvency suits.
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued three years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.
The total par value of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds in circulation at end-March was $939.6 million and lev-denominated bonds amounted to around 20 billion levs worth.
